note: Door beat as a conversation at the door. You can look at him and his parcel, ask questions, point him to reception. He pushes back. Ends map to v1 ids: door-hold, door-shut.

speaker.role: At the tower door · arms full

ask.say: Hey, can you grab the door? My badge is back in the van. I'm double-parked out there. Two seconds, I swear.

who.say: Finance, fourteenth floor. They're waiting on it. Come on, man, it's raining.

reception.say: Reception? Nobody's at reception this late. Just let me in, I'll be in and out.

push.say: Seriously? I do this every night, man. You're gonna get me fired over a door?

look_badge.label: Look at his lanyard
look_badge.look: No lanyard, no badge clip. A hi-vis vest that says SWIFTLINE. No company ID anywhere.

look_parcel.label: Look at the parcel
look_parcel.look: Label: HARBOR & CO · FINANCE · FL 14. No name, no tracking sticker, no carrier barcode.

look_reception.label: Look through the glass at reception
look_reception.look: Through the glass: the reception desk is lit and staffed. Someone's looking right at you.

reception.label: Reception's right inside. They'll sign you in.

close.label: Sorry, I can't let you in.

close_firm.label: Sorry. Reception will sign you in. I'm letting the door close.

tells.why: No badge, no company ID. "It's in the van" is the oldest line there is.
The parcel has a department but no name and no tracking. Real deliveries have both.
He said nobody was at reception. Someone was sitting right there.
He pushed back and you still let the door close. That's the hard part.
